token/grid: The KV cache keeps, for every token seen so far, a key and a value at every layer.
token/vec: Each key and each value is a vector of d numbers, as wide as the model. Here d is four thousand, and there are thirty two layers.
token/per: So one token costs two vectors, times thirty two layers, times four thousand numbers. At sixteen bits, two bytes each, that is five hundred and twelve thousand bytes for a single token: half a megabyte, or MB, where a megabyte is a million bytes.
grow/ctx: Now multiply by the tokens. A context of four thousand tokens needs about two gigabytes, for one sequence.
grow/formula: All together: two, times the layers, times the tokens, times d, times the bytes per number.
grow/double: It grows in a straight line. Twice the context, twice the cache.
grow/batch: And every sequence being served keeps a cache of its own. Sixteen at once need about thirty three gigabytes.
grow/weights: That is more than the model's own weights: about seven billion parameters, fourteen gigabytes at two bytes each.
fit/free: Now run it backward. Say that after loading the weights, sixteen gigabytes are left for the cache: sixteen billion bytes.
fit/per: Each token costs five hundred and twelve thousand bytes. So the question is how many of those fit into sixteen billion.
fit/fit: Divide. Cancel three zeros from each, and it is sixteen million over five hundred twelve: thirty one thousand, two hundred and fifty tokens.
fit/share: That budget is shared by every sequence at once: one sequence of thirty one thousand, two hundred and fifty tokens, or eight of about three thousand nine hundred each.
